featured_reviews.name: Jayesh Rao
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dear Team,

I am writing to express my extreme disappointment regarding the cancellation of my shoulder sonography appointment, which was informed to me merely 45 minutes before the scheduled time.

The reason provided was that the doctor was attending an emergency and would not be available for the entire day. This raises a serious concern — what kind of emergency lasts for the entire day without any backup arrangement being available in a reputed medical centre like yours?

What is even more frustrating is that the only alternative offered to us was an appointment on Monday instead of Saturday. We are working individuals and had managed, with great difficulty, to arrange leave from work specifically for this appointment. Because of your inability to honour the commitment given to patients, we are now forced to take another leave on a working Monday as well.

Additionally, we were informed that there is only one doctor available for sonography. Is this truly the strength of your medical network and operational preparedness? For a healthcare institution of your scale, this reflects extremely poor planning and lack of contingency management.

Due to this last-minute cancellation, we are now unable to secure appointments elsewhere for today, causing unnecessary inconvenience, stress, and delay in medical evaluation.

Such unprofessional handling of patient appointments is highly unacceptable in the medical field, where discipline, responsibility, and patient commitment should be treated with utmost importance.

I sincerely hope you take this complaint seriously and ensure that such incidents are not repeated with other patients in the future.

Regards,
Jayesh Rao

Absolutely unacceptable experience. I am bruised, in pain, and honestly shocked at how careless and unprofessional this entire blood collection process was.

The technician moved the needle around INSIDE my vein multiple times after inserting it causing severe pain through my hand and arm. My whole hand has been hurting since. I already had a visible bruise from previous blood tests and specifically told him to use the same vein but a different spot, yet he still pierced directly through the bruised area.

What made this even worse was the complete lack of basic hygiene and professionalism. He was going to draw my blood without alcohol swabs and gloves until I pointed it out, which is beyond unacceptable for a basic medical procedure. On top of that, he casually threw the vials into a bag instead of storing and handling them properly, making me seriously question the safety and integrity of the samples.

To end it all, he then tried to overcharge me. After paying 13,000, he said if you don’t pay me more I won’t send you the link to your results.

Would strongly advise people to NOT book with NM MEDICAL

Symptoms of Typhoid You Should Never Ignore

Typhoid is a bacterial infection usually caused by contaminated food or water. The illness often develops gradually and may begin with symptoms such as high fever, fatigue, headache, abdominal pain, constipation or diarrhea, and body aches. Recognizing these symptoms of typhoid early is important because delayed diagnosis can lead to serious health complications.

Fever Panel Test: Detect the Root Cause of Persistent Fever

A fever that lasts for several days keeps returning or is accompanied by weakness and body pain should never be ignored. Persistent fever can be linked to infections such as dengue, malaria, typhoid, viral illnesses and other health conditions.

A Fever Panel Test helps identify the possible cause of ongoing fever through a combination of blood tests designed to detect common infections and inflammatory conditions. Depending on symptoms and medical advice, the panel may include tests for dengue, malaria, typhoid, complete blood count (CBC), and other infection markers.

Many infections begin with similar symptoms such as fever, chills, headache, fatigue, and body aches, making it difficult to identify the exact cause without proper testing. Delaying diagnosis may worsen the condition.

If your fever continues for more than a few days or is associated with symptoms like vomiting, severe weakness, rashes, or dehydration, getting tested early is important. A Fever Panel Test can help doctors understand the condition better and guide the right treatment plan.

Dengue Test Guide: NS1, IgM & IgG - Which One Do You Need?

Fever, severe body pain, headache, or weakness during mosquito season may seem like a common viral illness, but these could be signs of dengue that should not be ignored. Understanding the dengue test guide: NS1, IgM & IgG, can help you know when and which test is required.

The NS1 dengue test is usually recommended during the early stage of infection, typically within the first 1-5 days of fever. It helps detect the dengue virus quickly during the active phase of infection.

The IgM dengue test is generally advised after 5 days of symptoms, as it helps identify a recent dengue infection by detecting antibodies produced by the body.

The IgG dengue test is used to check for past dengue infection or secondary dengue exposure. It helps doctors understand whether the infection is current or from a previous exposure.
Choosing the right dengue test at the right time is important for proper diagnosis and medical care. Delaying testing may increase the risk of complications, especially if symptoms like persistent fever, vomiting, abdominal pain, or weakness worsen.

Hormones play a major role in regulating metabolism, energy, mood, reproductive health, and overall body functions. When hormone levels become imbalanced, the body may show symptoms such as acne, sleep disturbances, low energy, excessive hair growth, or changes in appetite. Identifying the root cause early is important for proper treatment and long-term health management.

If you are experiencing these symptoms, certain diagnostic tests can help evaluate your hormonal health. Common tests include thyroid profile tests (TSH, T3, T4), estrogen, progesterone and testosterone levels. These tests help doctors understand hormonal changes and recommend the right treatment plan.

Ignoring hormone imbalance symptoms may lead to complications such as fertility issues, metabolic disorders, and ongoing fatigue. Early testing can help manage symptoms effectively and support better overall well-being.

When Should You Get a Blood Test for Chikungunya?

Sudden fever, severe joint pain, body aches, or fatigue during monsoon season may seem like a common viral infection, but these could be signs of chikungunya that should not be ignored.
Knowing when you should get a blood test for chikungunya is important for early diagnosis and timely treatment. Chikungunya is a mosquito-borne infection that commonly causes high fever, joint pain, headache, muscle pain, and weakness. Since these symptoms can overlap with dengue or viral fever, proper testing is essential for accurate diagnosis.

A blood test is usually recommended if symptoms appear within a few days of a mosquito bite or if fever and joint pain persist. Early testing helps doctors confirm the infection and monitor your condition effectively. Rheumatoid Arthritis Test: Detect Joint Issues Early

Persistent joint pain, stiffness in the morning, or swelling in your hands and feet may seem like temporary discomfort, but these could be early signs of rheumatoid arthritis that shouldn’t be ignored.

A Rheumatoid Arthritis test helps detect autoimmune activity in the body where the immune system mistakenly attacks healthy joints. Blood tests such as Rheumatoid Factor (RF), Anti-CCP antibodies, and inflammatory markers like ESR and CRP play a key role in identifying this condition early.

Rheumatoid arthritis often begins gradually, with symptoms like joint tenderness, fatigue, and reduced mobility. Without timely diagnosis, it can lead to joint damage, chronic pain, and loss of function. Early detection through a Rheumatoid Arthritis test allows doctors to start treatment sooner and slow down disease progression.

What is a Bone Marrow Test?

Unexplained fatigue, frequent infections, or unusual bruising may seem like minor concerns, but they could be signs of underlying blood-related conditions that require deeper investigation.
A bone marrow test is a diagnostic procedure used to examine the soft tissue inside your bones where blood cells are produced. This test helps doctors evaluate the production of red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets, and is often recommended to diagnose or monitor conditions like anaemia, infections, blood disorders, or certain cancers.

When routine blood tests show abnormal results, a bone marrow test provides more detailed information about what is happening inside your body. It can help identify the cause of low blood counts, detect infections, or assess diseases affecting the bone marrow.

Many people feel anxious about advanced tests, but timely diagnosis is crucial for proper treatment. Ignoring persistent symptoms like weakness, repeated infections, or unexplained bleeding can delay necessary care.

Kidney Function Test (KFT): Check Your Kidney Health Early

Feeling unusually tired, noticing swelling in your feet, or experiencing changes in urination may seem minor, but these could be early signs of kidney issues that shouldn’t be ignored.
A Kidney Function Test (KFT) helps evaluate how well your kidneys are working by measuring key markers like creatinine, urea, electrolyte levels in your blood. These tests provide important insights into your kidney health and can detect problems even before noticeable symptoms appear.

Kidney-related conditions often develop silently, and symptoms such as fatigue, fluid retention, frequent or reduced urination, and loss of appetite may only show up when the condition has progressed. Feeling constantly tired, getting breathless easily, or noticing pale skin may seem to be a part of your daily routine. But in reality, these could be the signs of low hemoglobin levels that shouldn’t be ignored.

A hemoglobin test helps measure the amount of hemoglobin in your blood, which is responsible for carrying oxygen throughout your body. Low levels can indicate anemia, a condition that can lead to weakness, dizziness, headaches, and reduced energy levels. 

Common symptoms of anemia include fatigue, shortness of breath, cold hands and feet, frequent headaches, and difficulty concentrating. These symptoms often go unnoticed or are mistaken for stress or lack of sleep, delaying proper diagnosis and treatment.

• Delay in my eye surgery

My doctor is available only once every 15–20 days, so this error may now delay my surgery by weeks or even a month. This concerns my eyes and surgery, which should never be taken lightly.
